en: Points of Controversy,
Great Fifty-Section,
Sixth Chapter
Is it the case that the four truths are unconditioned? Yes.
"Are there four refuges, four shelters, four resorts, four final goals, four states of immortality, four deathless states, and four nibbānas?
"One should not say so...
[as before] "...are there four nibbānas?"
“Yes,” [you say].
“Is there, then, among the four kinds of Nibbāna, highness or lowness, inferiority or superiority, excellence or deficiency, a boundary, a division, a line, or an interval?
You should not speak thus… [as before]… No, indeed.
Is the truth of suffering unconditioned?
Yes. Is suffering unconditioned?
It should not be said thus … [as before] … Is the truth of suffering unconditioned? Yes.
Is bodily suffering, mental suffering, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair unconditioned?
One should not say so... [and so on] ...Is the truth of the origin unconditioned? One should not say so.
“Yes,” [you say].
“Then is origination unconditioned?
You should not say so … [and so on] …
Is the truth of the origin unconditioned? Yes.
Are craving for sensual pleasure, craving for existence, and craving for non-existence unconditioned? [No.]
It should not be said thus ... [as before] ...
Is the truth of the path unconditioned? Yes.
Is the path unconditioned?
One should not say so …pe… Is the truth of the path unconditioned?
“Yes,” [you say].
“Then right view … pe … right concentration is unconditioned?
You should not speak thus … pe … .
Is suffering conditioned?
Yes. Is the truth of suffering conditioned? Yes.
It should not be said so … [as before] … Is bodily suffering, mental suffering, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair conditioned? Yes.
Is the truth of suffering conditioned?
You should not say so … [and so on] … Is the origin conditioned?
“Yes.
“Then is the truth of the origin conditioned?
“One should not say so,” and so forth.
Are craving for sensual pleasure, craving for existence, and craving for non-existence conditioned?
Yes. Is the truth of the origin of suffering conditioned? Yes.
It should not be said thus … [as before] … Is the path conditioned? Yes.
Is the truth of the path conditioned?
One should not say so …pe… Is right view …pe… right concentration conditioned? One should not say so.
“Yes,” [you say].
“Then is the truth of the path conditioned?
You should not say so … [and so on] …
The truth of cessation is unconditioned; is cessation unconditioned?
Yes. The truth of suffering is unconditioned; is suffering unconditioned? No.
It should not be said so … [as before] … Is the truth of cessation unconditioned? Is cessation unconditioned? Yes.
Is the truth of the origin unconditioned? Is the origin unconditioned?
One should not say so...
[and so on] ...Is the truth of cessation unconditioned? Is cessation unconditioned? One should not say so.
“Yes,” [you say].
“Then the Truth of the Path is unconditioned, and the Path is unconditioned?
You should not speak thus… [and so on].
Is the truth of suffering unconditioned, yet suffering conditioned? Yes.
Is the truth of cessation unconditioned, yet cessation conditioned?
It should not be said so … [as before] … Is the truth of the origin unconditioned, while the origin is conditioned? Yes.
Is the truth of cessation unconditioned, while cessation itself is conditioned?
One should not say so... [and so on] ...
Is the truth of the path unconditioned, while the path itself is conditioned?
“Yes,” you say.
“Is the truth of cessation unconditioned, while cessation itself is conditioned?
You must not speak thus… [and so forth].
Is it not to be said that “the four truths are unconditioned”?
Yes, it is.
Has it not been said by the Blessed One:
“Bhikkhus, these four things are such, not otherwise, not different. Which four?”
‘This is suffering,’ monks—this is real for you, this is not unreal, this is not otherwise...
‘This is the origin of suffering’...
‘This is the cessation of suffering’... [and so on].
‘This is the practice leading to the cessation of suffering’—this is true, this is not false, this is not otherwise.
These, monks, are the four things that are true, not false, and not otherwise.
Is there such a sutta?
“Yes.
“In that case, then, the four truths are unconditioned.
The Discussion of the Truths is finished.
